question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}({x}^{2}+1), & \,0\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}y, & \,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the joint probability density function $f(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}({x}^{2}+1)\cdot \frac{1}{2}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}({x}^{2}+1)y\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [0,1]\times [0,2].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8}({x}^{2}+1)y, & \,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
